_comment: Expansion 6: what the politics engine says of threats (world/threats.py): a beast brought down by a hero of the history, a dead king laid to rest by others, a place emptied by a doom, a place filling again, a gang grown bold, a beast killed in a lord's great hunt, an outlaw's band broken by a lord's riders (G.2), an occupied town freed (G.3). Hosts on the roads (G.7): armies and hordes marching to their sieges, the dead on the march, crusades, refugees.

threat_hunted: {hero} brought {beast} down at last, in its lair at {home}, and came home with its head.
The hunt is over: {hero} killed {beast} in {home}. The farms round about lit fires all night.
{beast} is dead. {hero} tracked it to {home} and finished it there, and will not say what it cost.
Word from {home}: {hero} has slain {beast}, that the shepherds feared for a lifetime.
threat_emptied: {place} is empty. Those who lived went in the night, and {villain} has the fields.
The last families have left {place}. Nobody would stay another winter with {villain} so near.
{place} stands empty: doors open, hearths cold. The people who are left say {villain} drove them out.
No smoke over {place} now. {villain} took too many, and the rest took to the roads.
threat_rebuilding: Smoke over {place} again: families have come back to mend the roofs and sow the fields.
Settlers are coming to {place}, some of them its own folk, some strangers, all of them hopeful.
{place} is filling again. The first harvest since the bad years is in, and the inn has opened its shutters.
The empty houses of {place} have people in them again: a smith's fire, washing on the lines, children in the lane.
threat_laid: The priests of {place} went up to {home} with bell and candle, and {villain} lies still again. The dead have stopped walking.
{villain} is at rest. Pilgrims from {place} sealed {home} with prayers and stone, and the nights in {area} are quiet.
A hermit went into {home} alone, and came out at dawn grey-haired. Since then the dead of {villain} have not been seen.
Word from {area}: {home} is shut again. Whoever woke {villain} could not keep him awake, and the dogs of {place} have stopped howling.
threat_gang_grows: {gang} has doubled its numbers: deserters, runaways and worse have gone up to {home} to ride with {villain}.
{villain}'s men rode through {area} forty strong. {gang} is no longer a band of robbers but a little army.
Recruits keep coming to {gang} at {home}. {villain} pays in silver taken off the roads.
There are more of {gang} every week. {villain} turns nobody away who can hold a blade.
threat_great_hunt: {lord} called a great hunt on {villain}: hounds and beaters went up to {home}, and its head hangs on a gate now.
{villain} is dead. The huntsmen of {lord} ran it down near {home} with a hundred spears, and lost good men doing it.
Word from {area}: the great hunt of {lord} found {villain} at {home} and finished it. The farms of {place} feast tonight.
The horns of {lord} were heard over {area} for three days. On the fourth, they brought {villain} down below {home}.
threat_broken: The riders of {lord} burned {gang} out of {home}. {villain} was hanged at the crossroads above {place}.
{gang} is finished: {lord} sent soldiers to {home}, and {villain} swung for it before the week was out.
Word from {area}: {lord}'s men took {home} by night, and the roads round {place} are free of {gang}.
{villain} is dead on a rope, and {gang} scattered to the hills. {lord} has had enough of tolls on its roads.
occupation_ended: {place} is free: those who held it by force are gone, and {holder} has it back.
The standards over {place} are down. {holder} rules there again, and the gallows in the square came down first.
Word from {place}: the occupiers are gone, and the town has gone back to {holder}.
{holder} holds {place} again. Its people took down the strangers' banners with their own hands.
land_blight: The country round {home} is dying: the grass gone grey, the trees bare in their season, the wells of {area} gone bitter. The people of {place} say {villain} breathes it out.
A blight has come down on {area}. Whatever grows near {home} withers in a night, and the herders of {place} are driving their beasts the other way.
Word from {place}: the fields towards {home} have died, every blade, as if frost and fire had passed together. No one has seen a bird there since.
The dead land spreads from {home}. The charcoal-burners of {area} say it creeps a field's width a week, and nothing they burn will stop it.
host_marches: {attacker} has called its banners: an army marches on {place}.
The army of {attacker} is on the road, and every road it takes leads to {place}.
{attacker}'s host has left its musters. {place} looks to its walls.
Soldiers of {attacker} on the march, thousands of them, and they say {place} is where they will stop.
host_horde_marches: The horde of {attacker} is moving, and the farms in its way empty ahead of it. It goes for {place}.
{attacker} has gathered every spear it has. The horde goes for {place}.
Drums in the hills: the horde of {attacker} comes down on the road to {place}.
Word runs ahead of the horde of {attacker}: it is bound for {place}, and it is not in a hurry.
host_the_dead_marches: The dead of {villain} have left the barrow. They walk the roads now, and they walk towards {place}.
A column of the dead is on the road, and {villain} rides at its head. Its way leads to {place}.
Shepherds have seen the dead of {villain} walking in a long line by night, towards {place}.
{villain} has called his dead out of the earth, and they march on {place}.
host_crusade_marches: {who} has taken up arms against {villain}: a crusade marches to save {place}.
The bells of {who} rang all night. At dawn its crusade set out for {place}.
Knights and pilgrims under the banners of {who}, bound for {place} to stand against the dead.
{who} has preached a crusade. Its host goes to {place}, to meet the dead of {villain} there.
host_crusade_arrives: The crusade of {who} has come to {place}. Its banners stand at the gates, and the town breathes again.
{place} has the knights of {who} in its streets now, and fires burning at every gate.
The crusade of {who} holds {place}. Let the dead come, its captains say.
Hymns in the square of {place}: the crusade of {who} is there, and means to stay.
host_crusade_holds: The dead came to {place} and the crusade of {who} met them at the fences. {foe} is broken.
At {place} the knights of {who} stood their ground all night, and at dawn {foe} was dust.
{foe} fell on {place} and broke on the crusade of {who}. The town stands.
The crusade of {who} held {place}. Of {foe}, nothing is left but bones on the fields.
host_crusade_broken: The crusade of {who} met {foe} at {place}, and was broken. Few came back.
At {place} the knights of {who} went down under {foe}. Their banners lie in the mud.
{foe} broke the crusade of {who} at {place}, and went on into the town.
The crusade of {who} could not hold {place}. Its dead have joined the other side.
host_crusade_cleanses: The crusade of {who} came to {place} too late to save it, but in time to lay its dead: the haunting is lifted.
Priests of {who} walked the empty lanes of {place} with bell and book. The dead do not walk there now.
{place} is clean again: the crusade of {who} burned what the dead left and blessed the rest.
The knights of {who} have cleared {place} of the dead. The living may come home.
host_the_dead_strikes: The dead came to {place} in the night, and by morning it was theirs. Those who lived fled.
{host} has taken {place}. Its people are on the roads, or in the dead's ranks.
{place} is empty: {host} walked in, and nobody stayed to stop it.
No smoke over {place}. {host} came, and the living went.
host_horde_strikes: {host} fell on {place}. The fields are burning, and the town is shut tight behind what is left of its walls.
{place} is beset: {host} is camped at its gates, and has burned all it could reach.
{host} came down on {place}, killing and burning. The town holds, just.
The horde is at {place}. Those who could not get inside the walls did not live.
host_refugees_flee: Refugees from {place} on the road to {to}, carrying what they could.
The road from {place} to {to} is full of its people: carts, bundles, children on shoulders.
Those who got out of {place} are making for {to}. There are a great many of them.
A long column of folk from {place}, bound for {to}, and nothing to go back to.
host_refugees_arrive: Refugees from {from} have come to {place}. They sleep in the barns and the churchyard.
{place} is crowded with the people of {from}, and the price of bread has gone up.
The folk of {from} have reached {place}. Some will stay.
{place} has taken in the refugees of {from}. Not everyone is pleased.
